statements.text:
"The A.I. companies… have a strong financial incentive to deny claims. Medicare plans to pay them a share of the savings generated from rejections."

Musk's AI shouldn't determine whether Iowa seniors have healthcare procedures covered or if they're left to fend for themselves. https://t.co/w6O7cbZzpa

For our third stop of the day, we sat down with members of senior administration at Jefferson County Health Center. I was so impressed with their “patients first, money later” values and their commitment to serving the local community. 

We discussed a range of issues, from the “big impact” they are feeling from Medicaid cuts to staffing shortages to the lack of nurse educators. 

We also discussed the dreaded prior authorization process. My view? If a doctor says you need it, that is your prior authorization. We don’t want insurance companies or AI to deny treatments your doctor knows you need.

Just finished our fourth meet and greet of the weekend!

I got a chance to meet lots of Iowans from Newton and the surrounding area, as well as talk about important issues like public education, water quality, ending corruption in Washington, and AI/data centers. https://t.co/aUW5xXuf2d
I believe no data center should be built in Iowa that uses up our water or electric grid — or that drives up our costs in any way — without our consent.
When you have the three biggest companies essentially begging for congressional regulation, that should tell you something.
statements.venue: Rural Restoration Project candidate tour, Fairfield, Iowa (Southeast Iowa Union)

statements.text: Local people in Iowa do not need to subsidize billion- or trillion-dollar AI companies [...] No thank you. They need to pay their own way.
statements.venue: Rural Restoration Project candidate tour, Fairfield, Iowa (Southeast Iowa Union)

statements.text: Had an early breakfast this morning with retired law enforcement officers from the area. Had a great conversation about the need for resources and training in law enforcement, the need to bring down the national debt, the challenges of AI, and restoring trust in our government. https://t.co/4VErgyYkE3

No data center should be built that is going to use up our water, use up our electricity, jack up our electricity rates here in Iowa, or hurt our communities in any way. [...] Certainly there should be some regulation of AI more broadly.
statements.venue: CBS2 Iowa 'Beyond the Podium' candidate interview

statements.text: No data center should be allowed to come into our local communities. Take our water, take our electricity, drive up electricity costs against local opposition.
statements.venue: Iowa Starting Line, remarks at campaign stop in Maquoketa

statements.text: I do want to make sure that those AI centers are not coming in and taking our water and our electricity and all of that. [...] I do think there needs to be, regulation of AI, I think Congress should act on that. And I do think that there needs to be a real safeguards put in place, for AI.
statements.venue: PBS 'The Cities with Jim Mertens' interview

statements.text: First of all, I don't, fundamentally thin that corporations should be left to police themselves, at all, whether it's AI or or something else. [...] And on the AI front, look, I mean, the corporations themselve are calling for this regulation. I think that is remarkable when you think that most corporations don't want to be regulated at all.
statements.venue: PBS 'The Cities with Jim Mertens' interview

statements.text: So they are seeing some real dangers. And I think they are they are very worrie about what their own technology is capable of. And so that should be a huge flashing red sign right there. So absolutely, Congress needs to take action on that.
statements.venue: PBS 'The Cities with Jim Mertens' interview
